common_name: Amy Dennis Azalea (Fragrant Lemon-Yellow Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; site in dappled shade to morning sun with afternoon shade.

directions: Bred by Dr. Eugene Aromi of Mobile, Alabama and registered as a cross of his AAP-1 selection with the Knap Hill hybrid 'George Reynolds,' Amy Dennis bears large, fragrant, light lemon-yellow flowers lightly flushed red-orange along the petal edges and bud tips, with a strong yellow blotch. It grows into an upright, rounded deciduous shrub well suited to a woodland-edge border in Gulf South and mid-South gardens. Plant in humus-rich, consistently moist, acidic soil in dappled shade and avoid heavy pruning, since flower buds set on the previous year's growth.
sources: Azalea Society of America - The Azalean, Summer 2003, "Named Aromi Deciduous Hybrids"
Azalea Society of America - Aromi Legacy Project

common_name: Bees Haven Azalea (Fragrant White Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; site in dappled shade to morning sun with afternoon shade.

directions: Bred by Dr. Eugene Aromi of Mobile, Alabama from a cross of (Rhododendron austrinum x R. alabamense) with a yellow Exbury hybrid, Bees Haven produces small, intensely fragrant white flowers with a light pink flush around the stamens and a strong yellow blotch, true to its R. alabamense parentage. It forms a compact, rounded deciduous shrub that draws pollinators heavily when in bloom in mid-spring. Plant in humus-rich, acidic, well-drained soil in dappled shade and avoid heavy pruning, since flower buds set on the previous year's growth.

common_name: Decidedly Pink Azalea (White and Cardinal Red Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; site in dappled shade to morning sun with afternoon shade.

directions: Bred by Dr. Eugene Aromi of Mobile, Alabama from a cross of two unnamed Aromi selections (KY-7 x NR-1), Decidedly Pink produces large, lightly fragrant white flowers heavily flushed cardinal red with a deep yellow blotch. It became one of the more influential parents in the later Aromi breeding program, passing its heavy cardinal-red flush on to many subsequent hybrids. It grows into a rounded, medium-sized deciduous shrub; plant in humus-rich, acidic soil in dappled shade and avoid heavy pruning, since flower buds set on the previous year's growth.
sources: Azalea Society of America - The Azalean, Summer 2003, "Named Aromi Deciduous Hybrids"

common_name: June Jubilee Azalea (Fragrant White Late-Blooming Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; site in dappled shade to morning sun with afternoon shade.

directions: Bred by Dr. Eugene Aromi of Mobile, Alabama from a cross of (Rhododendron prunifolium x R. serrulatum) with R. arborescens, June Jubilee combines three native species prized for late bloom and fragrance, producing small but intensely sweet-scented white flowers against dark, glossy summer foliage. Flowering well after most deciduous azaleas have finished, it extends the native azalea season into early summer. Plant in humus-rich, consistently moist, acidic soil in dappled shade and avoid heavy pruning, since flower buds set on the previous year's growth.
sources: Azalea Society of America - The Azalean, Summer 2003, "Named Aromi Deciduous Hybrids"
